title: 2025 full season recap with a 2022 retrospective
source_summary: The recap follows kickoff incentives, floor-supplied coral, 1323’s preplaced autonomous and L1 specialization, 2910’s backside auto and algae security, then Einstein. The author disclaims knowing who invented several techniques first. Its 2022 three-second-possession interpretation is disputed and must not become rule guidance.
transfer_analysis: The useful recurring pattern is a shift in marginal value as partners and opponents improve. Save the intermediate reasoning and failed predictions instead of rewriting kickoff choices as obvious from the final outcome.

title: 2023 retrospective: failure response and defensive leverage
source_summary: The commentator follows 1678 after an intake failure: test remaining acquisition, then switch to defense on major scorers. Flat bumper contact, wall leverage and release timing matter. Late denial depends on whether the opponent still has time for another cycle and balance. A suspected module failure is commentary, not a verified diagnosis.
transfer_analysis: A fallback role requires a functioning drivetrain, useful geometry and a driver who has practiced it. Do not attribute all lost opposing output to one defender.

title: 2024 retrospective: hybrid poaching against double passing
source_summary: The analysis contrasts 1678 with two passers against a single passer, cleaner and hybrid defender/poacher. 1729 pressures routes and changes targets rather than chasing one robot indefinitely. Source protection and long detours constrain the defender. The late amplification burst narrows the score gap; penalties remain decisive.
transfer_analysis: Map route occupancy, protected zones and partner capacity before generalizing a defense role. A third scorer can become defense only if the remaining supply chain still feeds the cleaner.

title: 2022 Einstein final 1: supply, pressure and late decisions
source_summary: The narrator connects 6672’s defense on 1577 to supply and cleanup demands elsewhere, then discusses 4099 pressuring 254. Late shot disruption, climb contact and the decision to keep shooting are interpreted in the context of a close match. Counts and intent remain commentator observations.
transfer_analysis: A two-ball game rewards either-side access and quick recovery. Evaluate late shooting versus climb using a distribution of cycle times and score uncertainty, not a best-case cycle.

title: Scouting analysis with Tableau
source_summary: This tutorial builds averages, phase breakdowns, scatterplots, box plots and shared selection filters. It emphasizes match-level context: the same average autonomous score can represent different capability and reliability distributions, and an outlier deserves match review. This is a 2024 tutorial using historical example data, not current Tableau documentation.
transfer_analysis: Store attempts, failures, roles and opponent conditions. Averages hide whether an architecture was limited by ability, task allocation, a breakdown or interference.

title: 2019 retrospective: 1073 tank defense and constrained space
source_summary: An outside-scope example examines 1073 defending 1114 through choke geometry and bumper leverage. The discussion of tank viability is a conditional argument about the game’s spatial demands, not evidence that one drivetrain is universally superior.
transfer_analysis: Keep this as a historical analogy. Translation speed, defender reaction distance, scoring orientation and corridor width must be re-evaluated for the target season.

title: 2025 kickoff predictions
source_summary: At kickoff the author considers rapid L1 specialists, high-level coral scorers, algae and deep climbs. The video anticipates reef saturation and collection defense, and warns that two coral stations constrain three autonomous robots. These are January hypotheses rather than observed season outcomes.
transfer_analysis: Preserve predictions alongside later evidence. A correct anticipated issue does not validate every predicted solution or timing.

title: 2025 week zero finals: collection defense
source_summary: The author analyzes 190/2877/5422 against 166/4909/1073, discussing early failures, coral-station interception and excessive chasing. The algae-specialist/defender idea is a forecast. The video anticipates denial becoming more valuable near saturation; it does not establish that prediction as the season’s eventual universal meta. ASR frequently truncates 4909 to 499.
transfer_analysis: A defender needs a recoverable position with multiple useful responses. Causing a detour can matter even without contact, but an idle station blocker can be bypassed by coordinated opponents.

title: 2025 first Israel event: 1690 floor supply and defensive counters
source_summary: The narrator connects 1690’s ground-fed autonomous with reduced travel, then follows coral-station defense and offensive switches. Algae scoring provides another useful task when coral access is contested. Bumper dimensions and simultaneous climb access are discussed. The author’s early reservations about floor pickup should be retained alongside later evidence of its success.
transfer_analysis: An offensive architecture gains resilience when the same blocked collection does not prevent every valuable task. Size must be evaluated with partners at the endgame structure, not only against the individual starting limit.

title: 2025 week 1: poaching, RP allocation and local efficiency
source_summary: Examples include 3257 taking opposing algae, 238 attempting late climb denial, different reef allocation policies and 3467 using the opposing processor to activate cooperation. The author compares a nearby lower branch with a farther higher branch using points per time. The foul-trading discussion is speculative and rule-dependent.
transfer_analysis: Separate qualification RP policy from playoff win policy. Do not turn commentator foul arithmetic into legal permission or ignore repeated/escalating penalties.

title: 2025 week 1 viewer matches: algae drafting and defensive geometry
source_summary: Examples include 148/3005’s undefended scoring, 1619 drafting algae specialist 3100 with 5903, and 427 defending 2539. Early climb commitments can surrender useful scoring time. The defense discussion contrasts long-side leverage, short-side escapes, visibility and reactive station switching. Proposed outcomes with better execution are counterfactuals.
transfer_analysis: Drafting a specialist changes the spatial allocation of the entire alliance. A low average contribution can become valuable when it frees higher-output partners and avoids a congested supply lane.

title: 2025 autonomous routes and partner compatibility
source_summary: The video compares 2767, 747, 3683, 2056 and 1690. Starting pose, first branch selection, station edge pickup, partner staggering and ground-supplied coral affect the available cycle count. A final half-cycle can improve the teleop opening. Proposed seven-piece possibilities are forecasts, not measured results.
transfer_analysis: Optimize the joint autonomous schedule. A nominally faster individual route can lose alliance points by contacting a partner or occupying its supply lane.

title: 2025 week 2: acquisition disruption and floor supply
source_summary: The analysis compares 1991’s station defense, High Tide/Rembrandts alternating coral and algae, Ontario coral displacement and Texas floor acquisition. Ground supply spreads the defender’s job across a larger area; visibility and available supply constrain the counter. Some team numbers are corrupted by ASR.
transfer_analysis: A robust funnel and a ground collector impose different defensive problems. Do not rate an intake independently of human-player delivery and the opponent’s access to the supply area.

title: 2025 week 3: 1323 floor supply, local branch completion and pins
source_summary: The author highlights 1323’s upright autonomous pickup and ground-fed teleop. Finishing nearby L3/L2 branches after L4 is argued to help alliances already capable of saturation. L1 placement geometry gains importance. Pin interpretation, station denial and coral herding are discussed, with several hypothetical extensions.
transfer_analysis: A saturation policy is unsafe to generalize to an alliance that will leave valuable branches empty. Rules commentary needs the dated official manual and Q&A.

title: 2025 week 3 viewer matches: Rush defense and processor variance
source_summary: The Sacramento example discusses sharing work across an initially assigned reef boundary. Rush supplies a defensive fallback after scoring failure. Michigan processor examples emphasize human-player misses and recycled algae as a possible upset route. The proposed six-algae crowding threshold is an observation/hypothesis, not a universal calibrated probability.
transfer_analysis: A high-variance strategy can improve an underdog’s chance without increasing its average margin. Its value changes with human-player skill, access to the processor and the opponent’s adaptations.

title: 2025 week 4: role switching, autonomous marginal value and human players
source_summary: WPI examples contrast 125/88 alternating algae with 2079’s interception and disciplined translation against spinning escapes. The author discusses 1153’s central coral-plus-algae routine and why L3 can retain the same autonomous premium as L4 when both reefs saturate. 5940’s human-player distribution and short cycles motivate later resource-denial forecasts.
transfer_analysis: Compare autonomous premium and time released for teleop rather than treating every raw auto point as an independent lasting advantage. A proposed future theft role remains conditional on supply becoming scarce.

title: 2025 week 4 viewers: endgame pressure, processor defense and RP tradeoffs
source_summary: The video examines pre-climb disruption, a defended processor specialist and guarding coral stockpiles. Its partial ISR DCMP qualification snapshot distinguishes missing the coral RP for lack of cycles from choosing higher-value branches to preserve a win. That snapshot is neither the final event ranking nor a universal district model.
transfer_analysis: A capability can be easy in isolation yet costly under win pressure. Give specialists an escape or alternate role when their scoring access is narrow and defendable.

title: 2025 week 5: floor supply refinement and contested rule interpretation
source_summary: Contra Costa examples discuss autonomous deconfliction, human-player delivery and algae removal. The video contrasts 4414/987 in Las Vegas, Ontario ground/funnel cycles and ISR L1 placement. The author explicitly requests clearer interpretation of coral launching and offensive pinning; those opinions are not official rulings.
transfer_analysis: Task order changes with remaining space, supply and interference. Use dated rules and official Q&A to decide legality, preserving commentary only as evidence of the uncertainty teams faced.

title: 2025 pre-DCMP synthesis and qualification pathways
source_summary: The synthesis revisits alternating algae/coral, defensive leverage and a defender’s escape path. It forecasts alliance construction and discusses New England district-point routes: strong results, a valuable second-pick role or accumulating enough points across events. Historical New England examples are not numerical Peachtree thresholds.
transfer_analysis: Choose a role aligned with the team’s qualification objective and realistic field depth. A specialist earns a place through compatible, visible contributions; it is not automatically rescued by a low EPA.

title: 2025 DCMP: lollipop auto, algae roles and PCH 7538
source_summary: The completed review covers 2910’s backside auto enabling a third coral routine, New England finals adaptations and PCH 7538’s acquisition defense against 1771/1833. It then discusses Ontario algae-first play and predicted Worlds drafting. Estimated defensive point denial and future division outcomes are commentary.
transfer_analysis: Target an alliance capability bottleneck, not necessarily the highest EPA. Keep PCH’s observed defense example separate from claims that the same skill would guarantee a Worlds division win.

title: 2025 pre-Worlds: drafting forecasts and algae counter-strategies
source_summary: The video uses a hypothetical Curie selection to explore offensive depth, defense substitutions and showing compatible autonomous. FMA team 11 illustrates algae theft and late climbing; Northstar illustrates choosing processor despite having a net shooter. Much of the drafting section is explicitly a forecast using assumed rankings.
transfer_analysis: Mechanism capability and chosen match role differ. Evaluate a specialist’s opportunity cost and available partner substitutes before translating a forecast into design advice.

title: 2025 Einstein finals 1–3
source_summary: The narrator contrasts lollipop autonomous routines, prompt algae security and later coral saturation. 2910’s algae steals in finals 2 and 3, 1323’s L1 stacking and a knocked-over L1 stack in final 1 receive attention. The argument about hidden score and drive-team psychology is interpretation; ASR score numbers are unreliable.
transfer_analysis: Treat theft as a conditional score swing, accounting for whether either alliance would otherwise score the piece. Preserve the opportunity cost, recovery and stacking stability of the L1 architecture.

title: 2025 Milstein division finals: three-match strategic adaptation
source_summary: The series contrasts 254/5940’s alliance with 118/Petey/324. The author follows defense in match one, triple offense in match two and a later defensive response. Processor awareness, uncollected algae, missed placement and L1 geometry matter. Explanations of pick intent and rushed-driver psychology are explicitly inferred.
transfer_analysis: A best-of-three gives evidence about adaptation, not three independent identical trials. A high ceiling architecture still needs repeatability and practiced alternate roles.

title: 2025 Daly and Curie: depth, declines and containment
source_summary: The author interprets Daly’s invitation/decline sequence and 2056’s lower-seed alliance through field depth. Curie’s example features 1771 containing 3005 after an algae incursion while partners continue scoring. Claims about why invitations were accepted or declined require team confirmation.
transfer_analysis: Compare full available lineups and pick order. Trading a captain’s offense for defense can be rational when the remaining two-robot matchup and penalty exposure improve the alliance outcome.

title: 2025 Hopper finals and an Einstein autonomous algae steal
source_summary: Hopper’s funnel cycling and 2767’s algae/defense role are contrasted with an opposing alliance’s responses. The Einstein example follows an autonomous algae steal against a changed opposing setup, alongside important breakage and substitution context. The author does not prove that the steal alone caused the result.
transfer_analysis: An autonomous counter needs a reliable way to recognize the setup and a safe fallback. A large funnel plus skilled human players can remain competitive with ground acquisition.

title: 2025 IRI finals: altered rules, theft and rescue costs
source_summary: The author notes additional algae and different selection order at IRI, then analyzes 2056/1690/4028 against the opposing finalists. Theft, a stranded robot, attempted rescue and containment change the series. Proposed conversions of offseason scores into Worlds equivalents are counterfactual estimates.
transfer_analysis: Keep offseason results in a separate ruleset. Rescue decisions trade a partner’s restored future output against travel, lost scoring and penalty exposure; nominal clean-score subtraction does not undo changed play.

title: 2026 kickoff: shift-by-shift strategy predictions
source_summary: The kickoff analysis centers on active-window preparation, passing, theft and timing the return from defense. It proposes depot/outpost autonomous and contests of neutral fuel, then compares climb time with available fuel scoring. Predictions about pin defense, passing and future play should not be presented as established meta.
transfer_analysis: Shift order changes inventory, starting position and recovery slack. Raw current score can mislead before both alliances have received comparable scoring opportunities.

title: 2026 build-season architecture, using 2017 as an analogy
source_summary: The author references 254’s 2017 hopper and roller-fed shooter, then argues that 2026 indexing, intake and sustained supply must keep pace with firing. Fixed shooters and turrets require different collection paths. Passing, choke defense and transition positioning are explored as forecasts. The video itself revises earlier ideas.
transfer_analysis: The old robot is an architectural precedent, not a dimensionally valid transplant. Retain publication date and later counterevidence when retrieving predictions.

title: 2026 week zero finals and driver visibility
source_summary: The analysis follows 6328/2877/2342 against the opposing finalists through three matches, separating breakage and beaching from tactical choices. Driver-station blind areas, intake failures, shift-order recovery and a braced 6328 shot location matter. Team numbers in ASR are inconsistent and require event-record checking.
transfer_analysis: A robot can exploit field contact for repeatable heading while accepting fewer transit routes. A match with failed partners is not a clean comparison of architecture strength.

title: 2026 Istanbul practice: 9483 preparation and mobile firing
source_summary: 9483’s practice-match example shows self-passing, a large hopper, angled collection and continuous mobile shooting. The author explicitly warns that the opposing alliance is incomplete; the reported 409 is not an official competitive benchmark.
transfer_analysis: A large buffer buys collection time, but capacity alone does not supply indefinite shooting. Re-test the policy under opposing resource theft and contact.

title: 2026 week 1: triple defense, resource loops and passing
source_summary: Pikes Peak examples connect triple defense and theft to a closer contest against 8044/498. The California example features 1678/9470/9584, staggered refill and a dedicated passer. Further examples discuss 27/5460 and 6329. Many numerical denials and intent explanations are commentator estimates.
transfer_analysis: High qualification output under weak contesting does not predict the same result under playoff defense. A passer changes both resource access and lane occupancy, not just fuel volume.

title: 2026 week 2: fixed shooters, turrets, geometry and PCH
source_summary: The author examines 254/9470, 1323/5940, 4414/973, 4946 and a PCH turret/dumper pairing involving 1771 and 1833. Topics include preload placement, hairpin returns, braced shooting, driver-station visibility, rounded bumpers and supply denial. A cited 17% endgame effect lacks a verified dataset here.
transfer_analysis: Treat the proposed two-turret/one-dumper alliance as a dated forecast. Do not substitute architecture labels for measured escape, supply or contact tolerance.

title: 2026 week 2 viewer matches: zone defense and original 2910
source_summary: 3467’s visibility-aware routes and 1807’s conservative trench marking contrast with defenders who overcommit. 195/176 illustrate coordinated scoring and refill. The original hopperless 2910 is discussed as supply-dependent, with optimistic projections about later partners. Those projections predate the team’s subsequent rebuild.
transfer_analysis: The 2910 sequence is useful counterevidence to hindsight: a plausible future alliance model may still fail a team’s nearer performance target. Keep the observed configuration and prediction separate.

How to Win a World Championship | FRC Strategy Analysis
source_summary: A complete available-caption study of the upper-bracket final and all three 2026 Einstein finals. The central account is the coupling of autonomous contact, transition position, neutral-zone supply, steal timing, shoot-on-the-move passing and 4065’s defensive geometry. Breakdowns and uncertain intent remain explicit confounders.
transfer_analysis: Compare whole alliance control loops, not drum rate against turret rate in isolation. A robot can make a smaller immediate score while changing who owns the next supply of fuel, who can arrive before a shift starts and which opponent must cross a defended bottleneck. The source’s counterfactual wins and point-denial estimates are hypotheses, not measured individual contributions.

title: How 254 beat their California counterparts at the World Championship! | FRC Strategy Analysis
source_summary: A complete available-caption study of 2026 Einstein match 3 (Curie–Milstein) and match 6 (Milstein–Johnson). The retrospective connects tall-dumper throughput to crossing risk, neutral-zone control, coordinated steals, 4946’s rounded perimeter and 6324’s flexible screening role. Its “lose auto by one” thesis is a conditional hypothesis, not a settled rule.
transfer_analysis: Architecture determines the set of routes available at a particular loaded configuration. Extended storage can turn a trench-capable robot into a bump-only robot during the exact interval when a steal requires escape. A partner that clears a crossing can be worth more than another marginal load, but the value depends on current inventory, shift timing and the defender’s recovery. Test these interactions as an alliance system.
